pool.text: In this problem, the variables \( x \) and \( y \) vary inversely. When \( x = 4 \), \( y = 16 \). What is the value of \( y \) when \( x = 2 \)?
pool.educational_aim: Synthesize Trigonometry & Additional Topics with related mathematical concepts to solve high-difficulty past-paper synthesis, optimization, proof, or modeling problems.
pool.exam_archetype: Trigonometry & Additional Topics — Non-Routine Synthesis & Past-Paper Challenge
pool.sol:
For inverse variation, the product of \( x \) and \( y \) is a constant \( k \):
\[ x \times y = k \]
Using the given initial values \( x = 4 \) and \( y = 16 \):
\[ k = 4 \times 16 = 64 \]
When \( x = 2 \):
\[ 2 \times y = 64 \Rightarrow y = \frac{64}{2} = 32 \].
hints: For inverse variation, the product of \( x \) and \( y \) is a constant \( k \): \(x \times y = k\).
Using the given initial values \( x = 4 \) and \( y = 16 \): \(k = 4 \times 16\).
When \(x = 2\): \(2 \times y = 64 \implies y = \frac{64}{2}\).
